description: Audit policy, security configuration, and security-control changes.

source.note: Availability depends on audit policy configuration and role (domain controller vs. member server).

1102.headline: The Security audit log was cleared
1102.plain_english: Someone cleared the Windows Security audit log. This erases the record of activity on this computer. Attackers do this to cover their tracks — treat it as an emergency unless you specifically requested it.
1102.technical_description: Security event 1102: the Security audit log was cleared.
1102.when: Time Windows recorded the log-clearing event.
1102.why_it_matters: Log clearing is one of the strongest single indicators of malicious activity — it destroys evidence.
normal_when: Authorized log rotation with a change ticket
what_to_do: Check whether logs are forwarded to a central system (SIEM) — retrieve from there
Initiate incident response if not authorized

severity.low: Authorized log rotation with change ticket
severity.medium: Cleared by IT admin without a clear reason
severity.high: Cleared by non-IT account, or followed by suspicious activity

1102.important_note: Central log aggregation is the only reliable defence against 1102.

4719.headline: The system audit policy was changed
4719.plain_english: The rules that decide which Windows events get recorded were changed. If audit is turned off for important events, attackers can act without leaving a trace.
4719.technical_description: Security event 4719: system audit policy was changed. Records the category, subcategory, and old/new auditing settings.
4719.why_it_matters: Disabling audit is a known defence-evasion technique.
suspicious_when: Audit turned off for logon, process, or object access categories
what_to_do: Compare old and new audit settings
If audit was disabled for important categories, treat as high priority

severity.high: Audit disabled for critical categories without authorization

4719.important_note: Read the AuditPolicyChanges field to know exactly what changed.

4902.headline: The per-user audit policy table was created
4902.plain_english: Windows built a table of per-user auditing rules. This is usually routine (happens at policy refresh) but can indicate audit policy changes.
4902.technical_description: Security event 4902: per-user audit policy table was created.

where.Computer: Machine where the table was created

4902.why_it_matters: Changes to per-user audit policy can alter visibility.
normal_when: Routine policy refresh at boot or GPO update
what_to_do: Check whether it correlates with an authorized GPO update

4904.headline: An attempt was made to register a security event source
4904.plain_english: A program tried to register itself as a source of security events. Legitimate programs register at install; unexpected registrations can indicate tampering.
4904.technical_description: Security event 4904: an attempt to register a security event source.
4904.why_it_matters: Unexpected event-source registration can indicate tampering with the event pipeline.

4905.headline: An attempt was made to unregister a security event source
4905.plain_english: A program tried to unregister itself as a source of security events. This can be routine during software removal, or an attempt to stop logging from a program.
4905.technical_description: Security event 4905: an attempt to unregister a security event source.

4907.headline: Auditing settings on an object were changed
4907.plain_english: The auditing settings for a specific file, folder, registry key, or other object were changed. This affects whether activity on that object gets recorded — turning audit off is a defence-evasion technique.
4907.technical_description: Security event 4907: auditing settings on an object were changed. OriginalSecurityDescriptor and NewSecurityDescriptor show the change.
4907.why_it_matters: Attackers turn off object auditing to hide access to sensitive files.
suspicious_when: Audit removed from a sensitive object (e.g. NTDS.dit, SAM, sensitive share)
what_to_do: Compare old and new security descriptors to see what was removed
If audit was disabled for a sensitive object, treat as high priority

severity.high: Audit disabled on a sensitive object

4907.important_note: Compare old and new descriptors for the actual change.

implementation_notes.verified_field: Only display a plain-English explanation when `verified` is true.
